commit_message:
Deprecate the X_of_Y keywords of wrap_kvs in favour of encoder/decoder (#92) (#216) [bump minor]

* Deprecate the X_of_Y keywords of wrap_kvs in favour of encoder/decoder (#92)

key_of_id/id_of_key/obj_of_data/data_of_obj still work and behave exactly as
before, but now emit a DeprecationWarning naming the replacement
(key_decoder/key_encoder/value_decoder/value_encoder), attributed to the
caller's line in all four wrap_kvs modes. dol's own calls, doctests and tests
use the new spelling (the suite passes with the warning as an error), and the
docs, CLAUDE.md, llms*.txt and the agent skills name it as preferred.

misc/codemods/x_of_y_kwargs.py rewrites wrap_kvs call sites (code and
doctests, dependency-free); it is what dependents will be migrated with.

* Review fixes: token-based codemod, falsy transforms, warning attribution

- misc/codemods/x_of_y_kwargs.py now works on tokens: comments and strings
  never count when finding a wrap_kvs call's end, only keywords at the call's
  own depth are renamed, and a rename whose new name is already passed in the
  call is skipped and reported instead of producing a duplicate keyword.
  Doctest examples and fenced python blocks are rewritten the same way;
  Markdown files only get their embedded code rewritten. The mapping is
  imported from dol.trans (one source of truth).
- _handle_codecs checks the encoder/decoder and codec keywords with
  `is not None`, like the X_of_Y path: a falsy callable was silently dropped.
- The deprecation warning skips every frame inside dol (not only trans.py),
  so Pipe(wrap_kvs(...)) is attributed to the caller.
- dol-dev-wrap-kvs skill: the keyword names and the is-not-None rule.
